name: Historic Centre
tagline: Republic Square, the cathedral spire and the brewery cellars
description: The old town inside the ring of parks that replaced the fortifications, built around one of the largest squares in Czechia and the tallest church tower in the country. Restored burgher houses, the brewery a few minutes east, and the whole of the city's restaurant and bar life within a short walk.
bestFor: Short and medium stays that want everything on foot and the brewery nearby
pros: Every restaurant, bar and museum within ten minutes
Park ring on all sides for running and cycling
Trolleybus and tram lines converge here
cons: The highest rents in the city

name: Bory
tagline: The university district, with woodland and a lake at the edge
description: South of the centre around the University of West Bohemia campus, a mix of student housing, mid-century blocks and newer developments backing onto the Bory woods and swimming lake. Rents are low, the student population keeps prices down, and there is more green here than anywhere else close to town.
bestFor: Budget stays with a running route and a lake five minutes away
pros: Low rents and plenty of student-priced food
Woodland and a swimming lake on the doorstep
Fifteen minutes by tram to the square
cons: Quiet and half empty outside term
Little in the way of restaurants

name: Slovany
tagline: Across the river, settled and close in
description: An established residential district east of the centre across the Radbuza, with a mix of interwar villas and post-war blocks, its own shops and a calmer pace. The walk to the square takes about fifteen minutes and the river path runs the length of it. Rents sit comfortably below the old town.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a normal neighbourhood a short walk from the centre
pros: River path for running and cycling
cons: Mixed architecture with some tired blocks

name: Doubravka
tagline: Eastern estates, the cheapest larger flats
description: A large residential district on the eastern side, built mostly as panel estates with supermarkets, schools and good bus links. Nothing here is picturesque, but the flats are bigger than in the centre for less money and the Bolevec ponds and forest are within reach on the northern side.
bestFor: Longer stays needing space and everyday shopping rather than atmosphere
pros: Larger flats at the lowest prices
Full range of everyday shops and services
cons: Nothing to walk to in the evening

name: Skvrnany
tagline: West of the works, plain and very cheap
description: A working district west of the centre near the Skoda industrial site, mostly post-war blocks with a straightforward local character and the lowest rents in the city alongside Bory. Transport into the centre is quick by tram. This is a practical base rather than a pleasant one.
bestFor: The tightest budgets, with a tram ride accepted as the trade
pros: Rents at the bottom of the Plzen market
Direct tram line into the centre
Everyday shops and a local market
